evidence: The hunk shows infraSchemaStatements() hand-copying the migration_quarantine and migration_log CREATE statements that 00002/00003 also define, so the duplication is real. The PR was closed unmerged as superseded by #129, which makes the missing reply moot, and the packet does not show whether the duplication survived into the replacement.
guidance_note: When a schema must exist both as a goose migration and as a bootstrap statement, source both from one embedded definition at the moment the second copy is written.

evidence: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS returns no error on an existing table, so a changed flag derived from 'Exec returned nil' reports true on every Open, and the hunk gates commitWorkingSet on that flag. The closing comment rejects the whole heal-on-every-Open design that produces this symptom, so the PR was abandoned without a reply.
guidance_note: Derive a 'changed' return from an observed state difference such as a probe, never from a DDL statement succeeding.

narrative: One Copilot round raised two real design defects in the heal-every-Open approach. The PR was closed unmerged as superseded by #129, and the agent's closing comment rejects the design itself on single-enforcer and dataflow grounds. Neither thread got a reply because the branch was abandoned.
guidance_observations: The closing comment preserves the failure-mode analysis for the successor work, which is the right way to close a superseded PR that still holds real findings.

evidence: The original Restore does filepath.Join(snapshotsDir, name) on user input with no check, so '..' or a separator escapes the directory. b547077 adds validateSnapshotName (Base equality plus parseName) and a table test of traversal names.
guidance_note: Before joining a user-supplied name into a filesystem path, require that it be exactly one entry the package's own List would return.

evidence: runSnapshotsNew calls Take before Prune, and Prune is where keep <= 0 is rejected, so a bad budget leaves a snapshot behind and then errors. b547077 rejects retention_budget <= 0 in config.Load, which is the trust boundary and one of the reviewer's own options.
guidance_note: Validate config values in Load, before any side effect, rather than inside the first consumer that happens to check them.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT b547077 flag is a false positive: that commit touched config validation and validateSnapshotName, while the time.Now()-only naming in Take is original PR code. Same-tick collisions are real, since the original tests needed time.Sleep between Takes. The a57e5e4 fix was check-then-use, though, and F6 shows that gap.
guidance_note: When a name must be unique across concurrent callers, claim it with an atomic create (Mkdir/O_EXCL) and retry on EEXIST instead of stat-checking.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the MkdirAll(dstPath, perm) in walkAndCopy is original code, not something b547077 introduced. MkdirAll and OpenFile modes are umask-filtered, so the fix adds Chmod after creation. The umask test it added imported syscall into an all-GOOS test file, and that caused F7.
guidance_note: When a test needs a platform-specific syscall, put it in a build-tagged _unix_test.go file from the start.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: ficloneOrCopy's OpenFile with info.Mode().Perm() is original clone_linux.go code. Its mode is umask-filtered just like the fallback path, and a57e5e4 adds dstF.Chmod on both the FICLONE and io.Copy branches.
guidance_note: When fixing a metadata bug in one copy path, grep for every other path that creates the same files and fix them in the same commit.

evidence: a57e5e4's reserveSnapshotPaths only stat-checks the final and tmp paths, while its own comment says 'cross-process races have no upper bound at all'. Two concurrent Takes can both see a slot as free. 0f27d80 replaces the check with an atomic os.Mkdir of a .reserve sentinel and adds a 20-goroutine concurrency test.
guidance_note: When a fix's own comment names concurrent callers as the threat, use an atomic primitive rather than a check-then-use loop, and test it with concurrent goroutines rather than a sequential loop.

evidence: a57e5e4, the F4 fix, added 'syscall' to snapshot_test.go's imports for TestCloneTree_PreservesPermsUnderRestrictiveUmask, and syscall.Umask does not exist on Windows. Before that commit the package's tests compiled on Windows. 0f27d80 moved the test into snapshot_unix_test.go behind //go:build unix.
guidance_note: After adding a platform syscall to a test, run GOOS=windows go vet on the package before pushing, since the package already ships a non-unix clone file.

evidence: The flagged commit 0f27d80 only touched reservation, so the flag itself is a false positive. The real cause is the F1 fix: its stated contract is that Restore accepts only entries List would accept, but it validated the name and still used os.Stat, which follows a symlink that List skips. 6fd4d83 switches to Lstat and Mode().IsDir().
guidance_note: When gating Restore on 'only what List would return', apply every predicate List applies (entry type as well as name shape), not just the name parser.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: runSnapshotsNew calling Take with no lock is original code, and 0f27d80 did not touch cli/snapshots.go. The fix extracts LockCommitPath and wraps both new and restore. It placed the lock at ws.DatabasePath/.links-commit.lock, the very directory Restore renames, and that caused F10.
guidance_note: When wrapping an operation in a file lock, check whether the operation renames or deletes the directory the lock file lives in.

evidence: 6fd4d83 runs Restore, which renames databaseDir, while holding a lock file inside databaseDir. That moves the lock away, and the deferred os.Remove(lockPath) can delete another writer's lock at the canonical path. The F9 reply even states the lock path is inside ws.DatabasePath. 2ad00a5 moves the lock up to the storage directory.
guidance_note: When wrapping an operation in a file lock, check whether the operation renames or deletes the directory the lock file lives in.

evidence: The agent concedes the bug: OpenForRead keeps a Dolt connection open after releasing the commit lock, so Restore can rename under a live reader. It deferred the fix to ticket r5v9.7 with a KNOWN LIMITATION comment (55e429b), arguing a lifetime shared/exclusive lock needs Store.Open changes outside the ticket's stated scope. That deferral is defensible.
guidance_note: When adding cross-process coordination for a filesystem swap, list every process class that holds the directory open (writers and readers) and say in the first fix which ones it covers.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW 55e429b flag is a false positive: that commit only added a comment to cli/snapshots.go, and clone_darwin.go is original. Apple's clonefile(2) man page documents cloning a directory hierarchy, which contradicts the reviewer, but nothing in the packet shows whether the fast path succeeds. The round came four minutes after the merge, so nobody replied.

The hunk shows Restore renaming databaseDir away first. If the second os.Rename(snapshotPath, databaseDir) then fails, it returns an error with no rollback, which leaves the workspace without a database directory. This is original code (the flag is a false positive) and the finding arrived after the merge with no follow-up shown.
guidance_note: For any two-step rename swap, write the rollback of step one on step-two failure in the first version and test it with an injected failure.

narrative: This was a long filesystem-snapshot PR where nearly every fix opened the next round. The collision fix was check-then-use (F6), the umask test broke Windows compilation (F7), the name gate missed symlinks (F8), and the commit-lock fix put the lock inside the directory Restore renames (F10). The agent accepted every valid finding quickly and deferred only the architectural reader-lock gap, with a ticket. The PR merged before round 7, so two original-code findings were left unanswered, one of them a real rollback gap.
guidance_observations: Rounds 2 and 4 existed only because fixes were pushed without checking them against the threat their own comments named (concurrency, the lock's location).
Merging before the requested review round finished left F13's real offline-workspace bug unanswered.

evidence: The reasoning holds: same-state start was previously rejected and now reaches writeStatusTransition. Whether that function records a status From==To change is in store.go:1068-1070, which the packet does not show. The thread was resolved without a reply, and the PR has a single commit, so no fix was pushed.
guidance_note: When a change makes a previously unreachable branch reachable (same-state Apply), read the downstream writer for assumptions that the old rejection guaranteed.

evidence: The same-state claim transfer is the PR's declared target-state contract, and the updated test asserts it on purpose. So the request for a guard runs against the design, and leaving the code alone was right. The thread was silently resolved, though, with no recorded reason, and the coverage suggestion for same-actor re-start was reasonable.

narrative: One round raised two findings about the new same-state start behavior. Both threads were resolved by the author with no reply and no follow-up commit. F1 is a plausible audit-log defect the packet cannot confirm, and F2 is a design objection the PR intentionally overrides.
guidance_observations: Silently resolving threads leaves no record of whether a finding was judged wrong or simply ignored, which matters most for a plausible defect like F1.

evidence: The fallback compares the raw in.TargetStatus to 'in_progress', while ApplyUpdate normalizes TargetStatus through model.DefaultOpen later (visible in #126's hunk). So any alias that normalizes to in_progress triggers the transition without the env-derived assignee. The PR merged 2 minutes before the review arrived, and nobody followed up.
guidance_note: Key behavior on the parsed state value, never on the raw flag string, whenever a parser downstream accepts aliases.

narrative: The PR merged 32 seconds after creation, before Copilot's only review landed. The single finding (raw status string versus normalized state) is a real gap, and a suppressed low-confidence comment notes a related whitespace inconsistency. Neither got a response.
guidance_observations: Merging before the requested review completes turns every finding into an orphan; wait for the review round before merging.

evidence: The hunk keeps fs.String("by", os.Getenv("USER"), "") while only hiding the flag, and the round-1 text quotes the PR description as saying the default was dropped to empty, so code and description disagree. The thread was resolved silently, and the packet does not show whether the second commit changed the default.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check each behavioral claim in its description against the diff, especially a changed default.

evidence: brandon-fryslie replied 'yes it's at my request', which reads as owner intent for the hidden flag but does not address the USER default contradicting the PR description. The packet shows no change to the default, so it is unclear whether the leak was intended.
guidance_note: Before opening a PR, check each behavioral claim in its description against the diff, especially a changed default.

evidence: This is the same USER default as F1, in dependency.go. The hunk shows it retained, and the thread was resolved without a reply or a visible fix.
guidance_note: When changing one flag's default across commands, grep every definition of that flag and change them together.

evidence: This is the same USER default as F1, in bulk.go (two sites). The hunk shows it retained, and the thread was resolved without a reply or a visible fix.
Round 1 reviewed the same commit eebabab and re-raised F1 almost verbatim. It is a duplicate review pass, not caused by any fix, and was resolved silently.
This re-raises F2 on the same commit eebabab and is not fix-caused. It was resolved silently.
This re-raises F3 on the same commit eebabab and is not fix-caused. It was resolved silently.
This re-raises F4 on the same commit eebabab and is not fix-caused. It was resolved silently.

narrative: This PR was authored by elton-prawn, not the usual agent account. All three rounds ran on the same commit eebabab, so round 1 duplicated round 0's four findings. Every finding is the same real mismatch: the description says --by defaults to empty, but every site still defaults to $USER. The only reply ('yes it's at my request') does not address the default, and all threads were resolved without a visible fix.
guidance_observations: One missed sweep of a single flag default produced eight threads; changing the default at every site, or deriving it from one helper, would have produced none.

evidence: The hunk shows `in.TargetStatus = string(model.DefaultOpen(in.TargetStatus))` as an unchanged context line, so garbage was already coerced to 'open' before the old lookup table ran, and the 'regression' framing is wrong. The real issue (lenient parse of user input, plus the redundant second DefaultOpen) stands. It was resolved without a reply.
guidance_note: When rewriting a dispatch that consumes user input, replace a lenient parse at that boundary with the strict parser that returns an error.

narrative: One finding claimed a regression in status coercion. The coercion actually predates the PR, but the lenient parse of user-supplied --status is a real pre-existing defect. The thread was resolved with no reply, so the incorrect regression claim went unchallenged and the real issue went unrecorded.
guidance_observations: A finding that is wrong about cause but right about the defect deserves a split reply, not a silent resolve.

evidence: execGatedReconciliation routed RENAME/DROP/UPDATE through the same driver that swallows 'duplicate column'/'already exists', so a real failure could pass silently. 084eb09 splits it into execGatedCreate (swallows) and execGatedMutation (propagates). The reply names 0c83bd9, the reviewed commit, as the fix, when the split actually landed in 084eb09.
guidance_note: When one helper's bool parameter selects between two error policies, write two named helpers in the original PR.

evidence: countUserSnapshots hardcoded "pre-migrate", duplicating migrationSnapshotLabel. 084eb09 exposed IsMigrationSnapshotName, but kept the same strings.Contains logic (causing F3) and missed the identical Contains in migrate_snapshot_test.go (causing F5).
guidance_note: When extracting a shared classifier, grep every existing use of the literal it replaces, and write the predicate against the producer's exact format rather than a substring.

evidence: 084eb09, the F2 fix, promoted strings.Contains(name, migrationSnapshotLabel) into a public classifier whose doc claims it separates user from migration snapshots. A user --label containing 'pre-migrate' contradicts that. 3260451 parses the label shape instead.
guidance_note: When extracting a shared classifier, grep every existing use of the literal it replaces, and write the predicate against the producer's exact format rather than a substring.

evidence: 3260451 validates only the text after the first '-', so 'foo-pre-migrate-123' returns true. That matters because countUserSnapshots feeds it raw ReadDir names, not List output. 75e08b2 requires an all-digit head.
guidance_note: When writing a predicate for a producer's format, enumerate every component of that format and validate each in the same commit.

evidence: The agent concedes 'I left the assertion in this test file behind'. 084eb09 replaced the hardcoded match in cli/snapshots_test.go but not the strings.Contains(snaps[0].Name, migrationSnapshotLabel) in migrate_snapshot_test.go.
guidance_note: When extracting a shared classifier, grep every existing use of the literal it replaces, and write the predicate against the producer's exact format rather than a substring.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 75e08b2 only tightened IsMigrationSnapshotName, while the unfiltered dbsnapshot.Prune in migrate() is round-0 code. Pruning the shared directory lets a mutating Open evict user snapshots. da9502e adds PruneMatching for both producers and a test with 25 user and 15 migration snapshots.
guidance_note: When a second producer starts writing into an existing directory, audit every deleter of that directory for kind-awareness in the same PR.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: da9502e did not touch hasCanonicalStatusConstraint, and the token fingerprint is round-0 code. The hunk shows it checks the epic token, the status set and NOT NULL, but not the epic arm's IS NULL, so the drifted clause passes. The 605fdd2 fix added only that one discriminator, which is what F8 then found.
guidance_note: When replacing an exact comparison with a token fingerprint, write a drift test for each invariant of the canonical clause before shipping the matcher.

evidence: After 605fdd2 the clause '(issue_type IN (epic) AND status IS NULL) OR (status IS NOT NULL AND status IN(...))' contains all four tokens, so a leaf arm with no epic guard passes. The agent's own reply concedes 'the fingerprint must encode every invariant'. 0ecb5ea adds hasNegatedEpicGuard.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one missing invariant in a fingerprint, enumerate every clause invariant and add all missing discriminators and drift tests in that one fix.

evidence: The matched = matched[:0] filter-in-place idiom introduced by da9502e (the F6 fix) is correct Go; the reviewer concedes it is a maintainability concern, not a bug. The fe58f46 change to a fresh slice is cheap and harmless.

The flag is a false positive: the manual set-and-nil of migrationPostSnapshotHookForTest is round-0 test code that 0ecb5ea did not touch. An early t.Fatal would leak the hook, and the agent notes a sibling test already uses t.Cleanup.
guidance_note: When a test assigns a package-level hook, register t.Cleanup on the next line, as the sibling test already did.

narrative: This PR wired snapshot-before-migrate into Open and took eight Copilot rounds. Three of them existed only because a fix was partial. The F2 classifier extraction kept a substring match (F3), validated only half the name (F4) and missed a second literal (F5). The F7 fingerprint fix added one discriminator where two were missing (F8). The agent accepted every finding, and every finding was valid.
guidance_observations: Both fix-caused chains were enumeration gaps: a format predicate and a clause fingerprint each extended one token per round instead of enumerating the full shape once.
The F1 reply cites the reviewed commit 0c83bd9 as the fix SHA when the change landed in 084eb09, so the thread record points at the wrong commit.
